issues.display_title: Issue #188: Exclude Public User Profile Route from Auth JWT Middleware
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Exclude Public User Profile Route from Auth JWT Middleware

Files Changed

  • src/middleware/auth.go
  • src/routes/v1/route.go
  • src/middleware/auth_test.go (new test file)
  • src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go (new test file)

Summary of Implementation

The AuthJWTExclude middleware was updated to support:

  1. Dynamic route parameter pattern matching (e.g. :username).
  2. Explicit auth enforcement rules using the ! prefix (e.g. !GET:/v1/users/detail).
  3. Safe rule parsing so colons in path parameters are not confused with HTTP method separators.

In src/routes/v1/route.go, GET:/v1/users/:username and OPTIONS:/v1/users/:username were registered as excluded routes, while !GET:/v1/users/detail and !GET:/v1/users/me were registered as explicit auth-enforced rules.

Detailed Changes

1. Middleware Enhancement (src/middleware/auth.go)

type excludeRule struct {
	method   string
	path     string
	isPrefix bool
	isNegate bool
}
  • Rule Parsing: Detects ! prefix to flag isNegate = true. Only splits on colon if the colon appears before the first slash (indicating METHOD:path), avoiding corruption of path parameter patterns like /v1/users/:username.
  • Two-Pass Rule Evaluation:
    • Pass 1 (Negate / Require Auth): If any rule with isNegate = true matches the request path and method, authJWT(c) is immediately invoked, guaranteeing auth enforcement.
    • Pass 2 (Exclude / Bypass Auth): If any rule with isNegate = false matches, c.Next() is called to bypass auth.
    • Fallback: Any path not matching an exclude rule defaults to authJWT(c).
  • matchPath Function:
    • Handles prefix matching with isPrefix.
    • Handles exact string equality.
    • Handles :param segment matching by splitting both rule and request paths by /, checking segment counts, and treating :param as matching any single non-empty path segment.

2. Route Configuration (src/routes/v1/route.go)

func SetupRoutes(app *fiber.App) {
	v1 := app.Group("/v1", middleware.AuthJWTExclude(
		...
		"!GET:/v1/users/detail",
		"!GET:/v1/users/me",
		"GET:/v1/users/:username",
		"OPTIONS:/v1/users/:username",
	))
  • GET /v1/users/:username (and OPTIONS) allows public access to the user profile without credentials.
  • GET /v1/users/detail and GET /v1/users/me are protected by the negate rules and require valid JWT tokens.
  • All mutating endpoints (PUT /v1/users/*, PATCH /v1/users/*) require valid JWT tokens.

Verification & Tests

Automated Tests

  1. src/middleware/auth_test.go:
    • TestAuthJWTExclude_ParametricAndPrefixRules: Validates that public routes, wildcard prefix routes, and parameterized routes pass without token; and validates that negated private routes and non-excluded routes return 401 Unauthorized.
    • TestAuthJWT_PopulatesLocalsOnValidToken: Validates that authenticating with a valid JWT populates c.Locals("sub").
  2. src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go:
    • TestUserPublicProfileRouteIsExcluded: Verifies GET /v1/users/:username does not return 401 Missing Authorization header.
    • TestUserPrivateRoutesRequireAuth: Verifies all 11 private user routes return 401 Unauthorized without token.
    • TestUserPrivateRoutesPassWithValidAuthToken: Verifies valid JWT token is accepted on /v1/users/detail.
    • TestExistingExclusionsRemainUnaffected: Verifies existing exclusions (/v1/room, /v1/viewers/*, /v1/additional/version/latest, /v1/exhibitions/model) remain public.

Test Execution

go test -v ./src/middleware/...
go test -v ./src/routes/v1/...
go test ./...

All test suites pass successfully.

Overview

Endpoint GET /v1/users/:username is used to retrieve a user's public profile (controllers.GetUser). However, because the entire /v1 group is wrapped by middleware.AuthJWTExclude, this endpoint was previously blocked with 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when accessed without an authentication token.

Problem

  1. GET /v1/users/:username is a public endpoint intended for visitors and frontend profile viewers without requiring login credentials.
  2. middleware.AuthJWTExclude previously only performed literal string equality (reqPath == rule.path) or prefix matching (isPrefix). A parameterized path pattern like GET:/v1/users/:username was treated as a literal string and failed to match dynamic username paths (e.g. /v1/users/johndoe).
  3. Under the same /v1/users route prefix, there are private endpoints that MUST require authentication:
    • GET /v1/users/detail (user's personal data, settings, billing)
    • GET /v1/users/me (checks authenticated identity against session)
    • PUT /v1/users/detail, PUT /v1/users/info, PUT /v1/users/profile, PUT /v1/users/setting
    • PATCH /v1/users/deactivate, PATCH /v1/users/is-back, PATCH /v1/users/fav-colors, PATCH /v1/users/json-version, PATCH /v1/users/avatar
  4. Naively adding a wildcard rule like GET:/v1/users/* would bypass JWT verification for /v1/users/detail and /v1/users/me, preventing JWT claim population (c.Locals("sub")) and breaking authenticated requests.

Goals

  1. Allow unauthenticated public access to GET /v1/users/:username and OPTIONS /v1/users/:username.
  2. Ensure all other endpoints under /v1/users (especially GET /v1/users/detail and GET /v1/users/me) strictly require a valid JWT token.
  3. Keep all existing exclusions (/v1/room, /v1/viewers/*, POST:/v1/auth, GET:/v1/exhibitions/model, etc.) 100% unaffected.
  4. Provide comprehensive unit and route integration tests.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/middleware/auth.go (enhance AuthJWTExclude with path parameter matching and explicit negate/enforce rules)
  • src/routes/v1/route.go (register exclusion and negate rules)
  • src/middleware/auth_test.go (unit tests for middleware pattern matching and authentication enforcement)
  • src/routes/v1/userRoutes_test.go (integration tests for public and private routes)

Out of scope:

  • Changes to controllers.GetUser or user model/database schemas.
  • Changes to private user action handlers.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. GET /v1/users/:username succeeds without an Authorization header.
  2. OPTIONS /v1/users/:username succeeds without an Authorization header.
  3. GET /v1/users/detail returns 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when called without a token.
  4. GET /v1/users/me returns 401 Unauthorized ("Missing Authorization header") when called without a token.
  5. All PUT and PATCH endpoints under /v1/users require authentication.
  6. Valid JWT tokens on private endpoints properly populate c.Locals("sub") and c.Locals("ls").
  7. All existing excluded routes remain completely unaffected.
  8. All unit and route integration tests pass (go test ./...).
